title: Monomial-ideal tensor injection in a completed monoid polynomial ring
statement:
Let $L$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $P$ be a finitely generated commutative monoid written additively, and let $n\ge0$. For any commutative ring $D$, write $D[P]=\bigoplus_{q\in P}Dz^q$, with $z^qz^r=z^{q+r}$. Put $R=\mathbf Z[P]$ and $S=L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Let $\mathfrak a$ be any ideal of $S$ and let $B=\varprojlim_m S/\mathfrak a^m$ be the completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with $R\to B$ induced by $z^q\mapsto z^q$. Let $I\subseteq P$ satisfy $I+P\subseteq I$, allowing $I=\varnothing$, and set $\mathbf Z[I]=\bigoplus_{q\in I}\mathbf Zz^q\subseteq R$ and $L[I]=\bigoplus_{q\in I}Lz^q\subseteq L[P]$. There is a $B$-linear isomorphism
$$\mathbf Z[I]\otimes_R B\ \cong\ L[I]\otimes_{L[P]}B,\qquad z^q\otimes b\longmapsto z^q\otimes b,$$
compatible with multiplication into $B$. The multiplication map
$$\mu:\mathbf Z[I]\otimes_R B\longrightarrow B,\qquad z^q\otimes b\longmapsto z^qb,$$
is injective and has image the ideal $IB=(z^q:q\in I)B$. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Proof (1)--(2) of lem-trf-local-term-locality: the Kato monoid-ideal Tor-independence input of ILO VIII 3.4.3, printed p.110. Agent-extracted algebra lemma for the completed models in VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70; retained parent Step 3 and initial exact sequence of Step 4. The tensor injection is proved by coefficient-basis comparison and flat completion; it is not a theorem stated verbatim in ILO.

proof.text: Put $A=L[P]$ and $N=\mathbf Z[I]$. For $d=0,n$ set $C_d=A[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ and $T_d=\bigoplus_{q\in I,\,\alpha\in\mathbf N^d}Lz^qt^\alpha\subseteq C_d$. Polynomial coefficient uniqueness gives the displayed direct sum. Since $I+P\subseteq I$, multiplication by $lz^rt^\beta$ sends $az^qt^\alpha$ to $laz^{q+r}t^{\alpha+\beta}$ with $q+r\in I$; thus $T_d$ is an ideal. In particular $C_0=A$, $T_0=L[I]$, $C_n=S$ and $T_n\hookrightarrow S$ is an injective $S$-linear map.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70 (PDF p.76): coefficient-basis description of the polynomial models; agent-written calculation before completion.

proof.text:
For $d=0,n$, multiplication gives $\gamma_d:C_d\otimes_RN\to T_d$. Its inverse is the coefficient formula
$$\delta_d\left(\sum_{q,\alpha}l_{q,\alpha}z^qt^\alpha\right)=\sum_{q,\alpha}(l_{q,\alpha}t^\alpha)\otimes z^q.$$
This is additive and $C_d$-linear: for a monomial multiplier $az^rt^\beta$ the required equality is
$$(al t^{\alpha+\beta})\otimes z^{q+r}=(alz^rt^{\alpha+\beta})\otimes z^q,$$
which is precisely $R$-balancing. Such multipliers span $C_d$. Multiplication followed by the coefficient formula, on a generator $(lz^rt^\alpha)\otimes z^q$, gives $lt^\alpha\otimes z^{q+r}=(lz^rt^\alpha)\otimes z^q$; the other composite fixes every $lz^qt^\alpha$. Hence $\gamma_d$ and $\delta_d$ are inverse. This uses neither cancellation in $P$ nor flatness of $L$ over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product: universal property and defining bilinearity relations, applied to the coefficient-basis calculation extracted from ILO VI 1.6.

proof.text: Choose additive generators $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ of $P$. The evaluation map $L[X_1,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to S$, $X_j\mapsto z^{p_j}$, is surjective: every basis monomial $lz^qt^\alpha$ is the image of $lX^\nu t^\alpha$ for an expression $q=\sum\nu_jp_j$. Thus $S$ is a finite-type $L$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat] to the given ideal $\mathfrak a\subseteq S$ shows that $B$ is flat over $S$. The ideal need not lie in the Jacobson radical; only flatness is used.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, first sentence; Tag 00MB, lemma-completion-flat (1).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] with base $S$ and flat module $B$, the inclusion $T_n\hookrightarrow S$ remains injective in $B\otimes_ST_n\to B\otimes_SS$. Use $\gamma_n$ of Step 2 and [lem-trf-scalar-tensor-cancel-base-change] for $R\to S$ and the $S$-module $B$ to identify the source with $B\otimes_RN$. The target is $B$ via $b\otimes s\mapsto bs$, with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Under these identifications the map is $b\otimes z^q\mapsto bz^q$. Finally the swap $b\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes b$ is well-defined by bilinearity and is its own inverse; it preserves the $B$-action. Consequently the map $\mu:N\otimes_RB\to B$ in the statement is injective.

source.place: Tag 00MB, lemma-completion-flat (1), and Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product; scalar cancellation as in Mathlib LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Tower.lean, cancelBaseChange and its pure-tensor formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-scalar-tensor-cancel-base-change] also to $R\to A$ and the $A$-module $B$. Together with $\gamma_0:A\otimes_RN\cong L[I]$ it gives $B\otimes_AL[I]\cong B\otimes_RN$. Swapping the two tensor factors as in Step 4 and inverting this isomorphism yields the required $B$-linear map $N\otimes_RB\cong L[I]\otimes_AB$. Its formula is $z^q\otimes b\mapsto z^q\otimes b$: both routes start with $b\otimes(1\otimes z^q)$. Explicitly the inverse sends $(\sum_q l_qz^q)\otimes b$ to $\sum_q z^q\otimes l_qb$. The relation for $az^r\in A$ follows from $z^{q+r}\otimes ab=z^q\otimes az^rb$. Multiplying either formula into $B$ gives $z^qb$, so the compatibility with multiplication is equality of the actual maps.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product; scalar cancellation in Mathlib LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Tower.lean, cancelBaseChange. Agent-written coefficient comparison in the ILO VI 1.6 models.

proof.text: Every element of $N\otimes_RB$ is a finite sum of terms $z^q\otimes b_q$ with $q\in I$, because $N$ is the free abelian group on those monomials and tensors are generated by pure tensors. Thus $\operatorname{im}\mu\subseteq (z^q:q\in I)B$. Conversely every finite sum $\sum_q z^qb_q$ is the image of $\sum_q z^q\otimes b_q$, proving the opposite inclusion. If $I=\varnothing$, both tensor sources and the image ideal are zero, so all conclusions still hold.
